slides.title:
On Black Friday 2015,
REI *closed every store.*
On purpose.
slides.sub:
And paid its employees to stay away.
The true story 👇

slides.title:
stores closed on Nov. 27, 2015.
*Plus HQ and 2 distribution
centers.*
slides.sub:
Announced on Oct. 27, 2015 by the
outdoor co-op REI, in a letter to its
5.5 million members (REI newsroom).

slides.title:
employees *paid*
to not work that day.
slides.sub:
The idea: spend Black Friday outside
with loved ones, not in the aisles.
The hashtag: #OptOutside (REI).

slides.title:
endorsements on social media
*right after the announcement.*
slides.sub:
Then 1.4M+ hits on social and 175+
organizations joining in. Online traffic
up 26% that weekend (Retail Dive).

slides.title:
sales growth for REI
*in 2015.*
slides.sub:
Web sales +23%. Membership grew by
1M+ in a year, a record (Retail Dive, 2016).
Closing for a day didn't kill the year.

slides.title:
REI makes it *permanent.*
Every Black Friday, closed.
slides.sub:
Stores, distribution centers, call
centers, HQ. 16,000+ employees paid
to get outside (REI, Oct. 4, 2022).

slides.title:
paid days off since
*#OptOutside began.*
slides.sub:
7,000+ partners: parks, nonprofits,
outdoor brands (REI, Oct. 30, 2025).

slides.title: As a member-owned co-op, *our definition of success goes beyond money.*
slides.author:
Jerry Stritzke
then President & CEO of REI
(REI newsroom, Oct. 27, 2015)

slides.title:
Everyone shouts "-50%".
*Stand for something.*
slides.sub:
REI didn't win Black Friday with a bigger
discount. It won with a clear stance.
You don't need to close. But be clear.

✅ Say who you're for, on your homepage
✅ Show why your price is fair
✅ Real stock, real delivery dates
✅ One honest offer > 10 fake ones
